title: Command-line usage
heading: Command-line usage
text:
Command-line usage Documentation index · Build configuration · Python Commands below run from the repository root after building with --features clp. ./target/release/baldes vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 25 --rank1
./target/release/baldes cvrp instances/cvrplib/A-n32-k5.vrp --capacity-cuts
./target/release/baldes hgs instances/R101.txt --population-size 50 --nb-iter 5000
 The first argument selects the instance type: vrptw (time windows), cvrp(capacitated, no time windows), or hgs (Hybrid Genetic Search heuristic).The routing commands read Solomon-format files and CVRPLIB (TSPLIB) .vrpfiles; the format is detected from the content. vrptw enforces time windows and service times;cvrp ignores them.CVRPLIB instances have no time windows, so they are solved as cvrp. They usethe file's distance convention: TSPLIB nint for EUC_2D, ceil forCEIL_2D, or the explicit EDGE_WEIGHT_SECTION (full or triangular). As forSolomon files, the root fleet bound is the customer count. Route-length limits (DISTANCE) and service times are not supported. Run./target/release/baldes --help for usage.

title: Command-line usage
heading: Options
text: Options Option Meaning --customers N keep the first N customers --ng N NG neighbourhood size (default 8) --reference-ng the N nearest customers, ties by index (the comparison setup) --rounding MODE distances none, nearest, tenth or ceil (default: the file's convention) --rank1 separate limited-memory rank-one cuts --capacity / --capacity-cuts separate native rounded capacity cuts in the Clp root master --two-path-cuts enable capacity cuts with Kohl's time resource attached (VRPTW only) --tree run branch-and-price for integer routing --nodes N tree node limit (default 10,000) --branching MODE native (default), ryan-foster, vehicles, or arc --no-strong-branching use fractionality instead of phased strong branching --no-diving disable strong diving --no-mip-heuristic disable restricted-master integer search --mip-nodes N node budget per restricted-master integer-search call --enumerated-mip solve complete enumerated node masters with HiGHS; requires --tree and the highs feature --no-enumeration no reduced-cost fixing or enumeration --upper-bound X initial incumbent for fixing --no-stabilization no dual-price smoothing --master MODE clp (default), highs (requires HiGHS), or native ipm; IPM disables stabilization --bound-mode MODE numerical (default) uses pricing bounds with tolerances; certified requires independent original-domain bound validation --hgs-time S positive HGS search budget before routing solve; separate from --time --hgs-columns MODE best plan (default), all distinct feasible routes, or N cheapest new routes --dynamic-ng P strengthen NG memories from master cycles at separator priority P --option NAME=VALUE set a supported BALDES pricing option (repeatable) --verbose, -v, --log solver progress table on stderr, every 10 CG iterations --log-interval N enable progress every N CG iterations; N must be positive --iterations N master iteration limit --time S routing solve or standalone HGS time limit in seconds --json FILE write root LP/history or HGS solution results --population-size N HGS minimum population size (default: 25) --nb-iter N HGS iterations without improvement before stopping/restarting --seed N HGS random seed (default: 0) --help, -h show all CLI options, including tree controls Root Optimal means the LP relaxation converged; tree Optimal means theinteger routing gap closed within the configured tolerances. HGS suppliesfeasible solutions without an optimality proof. Root LP route values can befractional, and NG routes can revisit customers. Normal root and tree solves use numerical bounds and skip the full certificatesearch. Use --bound-mode certified for independently validated bounds. Thatmode attempts validation when an exact pass can close pricing or the incumbentgap; failure leaves its selected bound unknown. Route-feasibility checks andexact pricing remain enabled in both modes. JSON reports bound_mode, the selected bound, and separate numerical_boundand certified_bound fields. An unknown bound is null. A numerical estimatenever substitutes for an unknown certified bound. A tree result labels theguarantee of its global bound; it does not report a global numerical estimatein certified mode. Root results retain both estimates when available. Solomon instances are in instances/, and a few CVRPLIB ones ininstances/cvrplib/. Enable --verbose for an aligned progress table with the restricted-masterobjective, selected lower bound, incumbent, gap, reduced cost, column counts,pricing phase, and elapsed time. Use --log-interval 5 for more frequent output. For advanced routing, see the branch-and-price tree guide andenumerated MIP guide. Build checks and test commandslive in the validation guide; benchmark results are inRoot benchmarks. For named pricing controls, see the BALDES option reference.Public option names start with BALDES, for example--option BALDESlabelDominanceStrategy=1. Rust exposes supported metadata inOPTION_TABLE; Python exposes Solver.option_names() andSolver.option_support(name). The public list contains 39 supported controls,plus two enumerated-MIP controls when both clp and highs are enabled.Scope can depend on the operation or configured cut family.

title: Python: pybaldes
heading: Python: pybaldes
text:
Python: pybaldes Documentation index · Command-line usage Commands below run from the repository root. Python 3.9+, Rust/Cargo and aC++14 compiler are required to build the default package from source. The Python distribution and import are both named pybaldes. It contains thelow-level Solver, Route, and Phase bindings and direct Rust-backed VRPTW/CVRProot solving. The default build includes the Clp master, built from the samevendor/ submodules as the Rust CLI: git submodule update --init
python -m pip install .
 import pybaldes

result = pybaldes.solve_root(
    "instances/R101.txt",
    problem_type="vrptw",  # or "cvrp" for CVRPLIB .vrp files
    customers=25,
    capacity_cuts=True,
    rank_one_cuts=True,
    time_limit=120,
)
print(result.status, result.lp, result.bound, result.cuts)
for route in result.routes:
    print(route.value, route.cost, route.nodes)
 Instance.from_file(path) reads Solomon-format and CVRPLIB .vrp files. You can also build inputsin memory: from pybaldes import Customer, Instance

instance = Instance("small", capacity=2, customers=[
    Customer(0, 0),  # depot, zero demand
    Customer(1, 0, demand=1),
    Customer(0, 1, demand=1),
])
result = instance.solve_root(problem_type="cvrp", capacity_cuts=True)
 CVRP ignores time windows and service times; in-memory VRPTW data requires finiteready/due windows, including the depot. vehicles is retained as inputmetadata; the current root model uses the customer count as its fleet upperbound, matching the Rust CLI.

title: Python: pybaldes
heading: Solve options and results
text:
Solve options and results Options include ng, reference_ng, rounding (none, nearest, tenth, ceil),stabilize, reduced_cost_fixing, upper_bound, max_iterations,max_cut_rounds, and a pricing_options dictionary of BALDES option values.Disabling reduced-cost fixing also disables enumeration. Results include positiveLP routes, duals, iteration history, cut/fixing counts, and timers;result.to_dict() and result.to_json() export them. to_dict() retainsinfinite values; to_json() converts non-finite values to null.Cut counts include generated rows later retired.These are root LP relaxations; Optimal does not certify an integer VRP optimum. Option Default Meaning master_solver "clp" Select "clp", native "ipm", or "highs" (requires its build feature); IPM disables stabilization bound_mode "numerical" Use numerical pricing bounds, or "certified" for independent original-domain bound validation verbose False Print column-generation progress to stderr log_interval 10 Positive iteration interval for progress when verbose hgs_time None Positive HGS search budget in seconds before the root solve, separate from time_limit hgs_columns "best" Seed the best plan, "all" validated encountered routes, or a positive integer of cheapest new routes hgs_seed 0 Random seed for HGS seeding result.bound_mode identifies the selected result.bound guarantee.result.numerical_bound and result.certified_bound are separate: unknowncertificates remain negative infinity (null in JSON), even when a numericalestimate is finite. Normal mode skips certificate searches; exact pricing androute-feasibility validation remain enabled. Certified mode requests a boundwhen pricing or the incumbent gap may close. Failure never promotes thenumerical estimate to a certificate. For example, seed a native IPM root solve with HGS and log progress: result = pybaldes.solve_root(
    "instances/R101.txt", customers=25,
    master_solver="ipm", hgs_time=2, hgs_columns="all", verbose=True,
)
print(result.to_json())
 Python root solves enable Kohl with two_path_cuts=True. This attaches timeresource 0 for capacity-cut registration;ordinary capacity cuts retain the default resource -1. Both use the capacityfamily's priority 3 at root and 1 below it, complement form and persistent subset pool.

title: Algorithms and references
heading: Solver components
text: Solver components Bucket-graph labeling: resource and NG preparation, bucket grids, stronglyconnected component ordering, jump arcs, preceding-bucket dominance,bidirectional search with a moving half-way point, and symmetric joins. Staged pricing with the native heuristic phase schedule. Reduced-cost fixing on bucket arcs and elementary route enumeration withinspection pricing at the root and descendant nodes. Limited-memory rank-one (subset-row) cuts: 1- and 3-row separation,local-search and tuple-based 4- and 5-row separation, cut memory, andlimited- and full-memory cut state in pricing and enumeration labels. Dual-price smoothing, and a Clp-backed restricted master with cut rounds,basic-cut removal and artificial-column penalties; optional native IPM master solves. Rounded capacity and Kohl 2-path cuts, with time-window feasibility checks;strong k-path and route-load knapsack cuts integrated with pricing,enumeration, and inherited master rows. Solomon VRPTW and CVRPLIB CVRP input, HGS heuristic, initial-column seeding, and root solving. Dynamic NG strengthening from master cycles at configurable separator priority. The core solver uses only the Rust standard library. The clp feature linksCOIN-OR Clp through its C interface for the restricted master. The optionalhighs feature adds a HiGHS LP backend and integer solving.

title: Algorithms and references
heading: Additional cut configuration
text: Additional cut configuration Strong k-path and route-load knapsack cuts are available in the Rust root APIthrough with_kpath_cuts and with_knapsack_cuts. The latter takes originalinteger resource rows; KnapsackCutConfig::with_resource_indices maps originalresource IDs to solver coordinates. Load-dependent costs and that mapping passthrough pricing, enumeration, and inherited master rows.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Direct Cargo builds
text:
Direct Cargo builds Install Rust/Cargo and clone the repository. The core library can be builtwithout an external LP backend: cargo build --release
 For the CLI and routing master, initialize the vendored dependencies and buildwith Clp. This requires a C++14 compiler: git submodule update --init vendor/Clp vendor/CoinUtils
cargo build --release --features clp
./target/release/baldes --help
 The clp feature builds Clp 1.17.10 and CoinUtils 2.11 from those submodules.To also enable the optional HiGHS backend and integer solver, install itsshared library and use cargo build --release --features clp,highs.The CLI and routing tree require clp; highs alone provides the library'sHiGHS backend and generic MIP API. See below for library discovery details. Python installation is covered in the pybaldes guide.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Interactive configuration
text:
Interactive configuration From the repository root: make config       # Open the configuration window in your terminal
make              # Compile with the saved settings
 make menuconfig opens the same window. Use Up/Down or J/K to selectan option, Space/Enter to change it, S to save and exit, and Q/Escapeto discard changes. Text fields accept Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel,Backspace to delete and Ctrl-U to clear. Resize to at least 65 columns by 22rows; press a key after resizing to refresh the view. This is a kernel-style terminal menu, implemented in Rust rather than Linux'sKconfig tooling. It requires Make, Rust/Cargo, and POSIX stty in an interactiveANSI terminal (Linux/macOS). It opens in the current terminal; no desktopsession, Python packages, ncurses headers or UI library downloads are needed.The helper is compiled directly with rustc into target/baldes-build beforeconfiguration, so it does not need to build the solver first.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Build options
text:
Build options Setting Default Effect Profile release Choose Cargo's release or dev profile Clp Off Enable the clp Cargo feature HiGHS Off Enable the highs Cargo feature Command-line program Off Build the baldes executable along with the library; selects Clp Native CPU Off Add -C target-cpu=native, preserving existing Rust flags Release debug symbols Off Set CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=1 for profiling Offline Off Pass --offline to Cargo Locked dependencies On Pass --locked, preserving Cargo.lock Parallel jobs 0 (automatic) Pass --jobs N when nonzero Target triple Empty (host) Pass --target TRIPLE for cross compilation HiGHS installation Empty (automatic) Set HIGHS_DIR to the root containing lib/libhighs The library, including native IPM, pricing, cuts, and HGS, is always included.These components currently have no Cargo feature switches. Algorithm settingssuch as cut priorities and IPM tolerances remain runtime options. The CLI requires Clp. Selecting the CLI enables Clp; deselecting Clp alsodeselects the CLI. Native CPU optimization cannot be combined with a targettriple. Cross compilation requires installing the Rust target and configuringits linker separately, including any enabled native solver libraries. Before building Clp, initialize its source submodules and provide a C++14compiler: git submodule update --init vendor/Clp vendor/CoinUtils
 HiGHS needs a shared library with 32-bit HighsInt. Discovery follows theexisting Cargo build: HIGHS_DIR/lib, vendor/highs/lib, pkg-config, then thesystem linker path. Leaving the menu's installation field empty preservesHIGHS_DIR from your shell. Configure your runtime library search path asneeded for a custom HiGHS installation.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Saved settings and automation
text:
Saved settings and automation The menu saves a local .config, ignored by Git. Subsequent Make commandsread it. A missing configuration uses release/library-only defaults with nooptional solver dependencies. Cargo commands invoked directly continue touse their explicit Cargo flags; they do not read .config. make showconfig                # Display effective settings
make print-command             # Preview the Cargo build invocation
make defconfig                 # Replace .config with defaults
make defconfig CONFIG=ci.config # Write another configuration file
make CONFIG=ci.config          # Build with it
 For noninteractive use, run make defconfig and edit the file or supply asaved config via CONFIG=path. The format is CONFIG_NAME=value, using y/nfor booleans and double quotes for strings. Backslashes and quotes in stringsmust be escaped. Missing settings take their defaults; unknown/duplicate keys,invalid values and conflicting dependencies are rejected. The file is parsedas data and is never included as Make code or sourced by a shell. An example configuration for the CLI with both LP backends: CONFIG_PROFILE=release
CONFIG_CLP=y
CONFIG_HIGHS=y
CONFIG_CLI=y
CONFIG_NATIVE_CPU=n
CONFIG_RELEASE_DEBUG=n
CONFIG_OFFLINE=n
CONFIG_LOCKED=y
CONFIG_JOBS=0
CONFIG_TARGET=""
CONFIG_HIGHS_DIR=""

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
text: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle Documentation index · Branching ·Enumerated MIP The Rust tree solves a routing set-partitioning master with one pricing graph.It requires nonnegative arc costs and unique public arc IDs. The base rows area fleet upper bound and one equality per customer; the tree validates thisstructure before searching.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Run a tree

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Node processing
text: Node processing The search selects a node by its lower bound and evaluates it within theremaining global budget. Its main steps are: Construct the root master, or fork the solved parent and append the child'sconstraints. Run column generation, pricing, cut rounds, and enabled fixing/enumeration. Share valid elementary routes with the incumbent heuristic and other nodes. Search restricted columns for a feasible integer solution; optionally runHiGHS over a complete enumerated universe. Close the node when its selected bound meets the incumbent gap, or selecta branching candidate and create children. Strong trials and diving useisolated evaluations. Time limits are cooperative across solver operations. A backend call canfinish after its requested budget. Limits preserve bounds for unfinished nodes. options.root.bound_mode selects BoundMode::Numerical by default, orBoundMode::Certified for independent original-domain validation. The CLIequivalent is --bound-mode numerical|certified. Numerical bounds authorizeordinary pruning within the configured tolerances. Certified mode never usesa numerical estimate to close a node: an unsuccessful certificate attemptleaves the bound unknown. TreeOutput::bound_mode and JSON label the boundand the guarantee of gap-based termination. Warm starts retain the two boundsseparately, so changing modes cannot promote a parent's numerical estimate.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: What a child inherits
text: What a child inherits State Child handling Clp master Deep-copy model, basis, solution, scaling, and simplex state Branch and cut rows Preserve physical rows and coefficient mappings; append new branch rows Existing route columns Retain coefficients and upper bounds; retire routes outside the new domain Pricing graph Carry bucket preparation, fixed bucket arcs, NG state, options, and adaptive state Labels Rebuild for the child's duals and active branch resources Enumeration Retain/filter routes where compatible and preserve branch-distinct arc paths Sibling state Own independent mutable models and pricing state When enumeration changes the master to full-memory cut coefficients, existingcolumns are updated as well as new ones. Reusing limited-memory coefficientsfor only part of the enumerated master would change the model.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Root snapshots and manual inheritance
text: Root snapshots and manual inheritance Set RootOptions::capture_state = true to retain a solved NodeSnapshot inRootOutput::snapshot. The tree arranges snapshot capture for its own nodes.Manual callers use root::inherit_branches(parent, additional_branches, options)for typed constraints, or root::inherit for arc-flow tuples. Supply only theadditional branches; the parent already contains its ancestor rows.To retain the child's snapshot for another generation, enable capture on thatsolve too. Snapshots retain both restricted-master columns and the generated column pool,including cached columns that have not entered the master. Child branch rowsand cut cleanup update cached coefficients as well as loaded coefficients.Regeneration checks the child's current path restrictions; a cached route isnot automatically admissible. Manually constructed column-generationWarmStart values provide generated_pool in creation order; an empty pool isinitialized from the loaded columns. The snapshot exposes bound_mode(), branch_depth(), active_cuts(), andenumerated_routes(). A route count alone does not establish completeness;the enumerated-MIP adapter separately checks the completion flag.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Incumbents, proofs, and status
text: Incumbents, proofs, and status Source Supplies an incumbent? Certifies the routing lower bound? Validated elementary route solution Yes No, by its objective alone Restricted-column integer heuristic Yes, after validation No Exact node pricing When the resulting routes form an integer witness Numerical estimate in normal mode; independent certificate required in certified mode Heuristic strong trial or dive Can find a witness No proof for the original node Complete enumerated HiGHS MIP Yes, after validation Only within saved enumeration coverage and for proved outcomes A cost-only --upper-bound can assist root fixing, but the tree needs actualfeasible routes before accepting an incumbent. It does not invent a solutionfrom the supplied number. Optimal means the configured numerical gap is closed. TimeLimit,NodeLimit, and Incomplete retain unfinished-node bounds. Check whether afinite incumbent and routes are present before treating a limited run as asolution. JSON encodes nonfinite numbers as null. The restricted-column heuristic uses TreeOptions::mip_node_limit andmip_time_limit; CLI --mip-nodes budgets that heuristic. Optional HiGHS nodeMIP has separate controls and counters; see Enumerated MIP.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Limits and validation
text: Limits and validation Every root, child, and priced trial runs node preprocessing before columngeneration. A worklist propagates continuous bounds through the originalarc-flow master rows and flow conservation, including equivalent outgoingcover rows. Child nodes also propagate active inherited capacity, complement,and two-path cut rows using their exact additive arc coefficients and currentphysical row bounds. Retired cut rows are excluded. Contradictions certify node infeasibility without LP solving orpricing. Zero upper bounds retire inherited columns and restrict both pricingdirections and complete enumeration. Positive aggregate lower bounds remainenforced by their original master rows; they do not require every route tocontain the arc. Parent and sibling state remains independent. RootOutput::preprocessing reports bound updates, processed rows,infeasibility, and whether the bounded worklist reached completion. Reachingthe work limit keeps valid deductions and continues ordinary node evaluation.The reusable master::preprocessing engine accepts signed sparse rows andinfinite variable bounds, but callers must supply a complete formulation.Applying it to an unfinished restricted-column master would be unsound. Ryan–Foster preprocessing closes transitive together groups, excludes arcsbetween apart groups, and fixes all incident arcs of an internally contradictorygroup to zero. Covering and assignment rows then determine whether that groupis mandatory and the node is infeasible. Pricing resources still enforce thecomplete route-level rules; preprocessing does not replace them. Preprocessing currently covers the single-network routing model. The boundedactivity worklist may leave contradictions that require solving the LP.Decomposition-wide local/global multiplicity links remain outside this adapter.

heading: Explicit fixed partial solutions

title: Routing branching
heading: Routing branching
text: Routing branching Documentation index · Tree lifecycle The tree branches on aggregate route quantities. Each child receives a typedconstraint, inherited master rows, and a compatible pricing domain. Thestandard routing model uses customer vertices as packing sets and enforcesunit customer coverage with equality rows.

title: Routing branching
heading: Choosing families
text:
Choosing families CLI mode Candidate families, in priority order --branching native (default) Vehicle count, packing-set assignment, Ryan–Foster, arc flow --branching vehicles Vehicle count, then arc-flow fallback --branching ryan-foster Ryan–Foster, then arc-flow fallback --branching arc Arc flow The selector uses the first enabled family with fractional candidates. Withinan applicable family it orders candidates by closeness of the fractional partto 0.5, with stable ties. Phased strong branching then evaluates candidateswhen enabled. These are adapter priorities, not a combined ranking across allfamilies. cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- \
  vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 10 --tree \
  --branching ryan-foster --time 60
 Rust configures the family flags through TreeOptions::branching, whose typeis BranchingOptions. Arc flow remains the fallback when all flags are false.

title: Routing branching
heading: Number of vehicles
text:
Number of vehicles Let v be the sum of LP values of nonempty routes in the selected network.For fractional v, the children enforce: down: number of nonempty routes <= floor(v)
up:   number of nonempty routes >= ceil(v)
 Pricing receives this row through nonempty-route return arcs to the sink.The split-depot source-to-sink arc contributes zero to this branch. Theoriginal fleet upper bound remains in the master.

title: Routing branching
heading: Ryan–Foster
text: Ryan–Foster For customers i and j, let w(i,j) be the sum of LP route values for routesvisiting both customers. When 0 < w(i,j) < 1, the children require: Child Allowed routes Apart A route can visit at most one of the pair Together A route visits both customers or neither Both children work with a single pricing network. The together conditionapplies to each route, rather than merely requiring both customers somewherein the final solution. Binary resources enforce the rule during labeling and bidirectional joins.Retained enumeration is filtered by the same rule. Existing NG routes thatrepeat a pair endpoint are retired from the child master. A violation row alsokeeps inherited and newly added master columns consistent with the branch. An apart constraint consumes one binary resource; a together constraintconsumes three. The current representation holds 512 resources. Candidategeneration skips already-branched pairs and falls back to arc flow when itcannot reserve resources for both Ryan–Foster children.

title: Routing branching
heading: Packing-set assignment
text: Packing-set assignment This family branches on assigning a customer packing set to a particularpricing network. If its fractional assignment to network k is y, thechildren enforce assignment to that network as zero or at least one.For example, in a heterogeneous fleet this could decide whether customer 7uses the small-vehicle network. The current tree has one network. Its customer equality rows already fixeach assignment to one. Assignment constraints can be constructed and enforced,but the normal single-network LP has no fractional assignment candidate. Anunassigned child for a mandatory customer is infeasible. Useful assignment branching requires multiple route families/networks,network-specific costs and resources, and master columns carrying the networkidentity. Setting a graph ID alone does not add that modeling support.

title: Routing branching
heading: Directed arc flow
text: Directed arc flow For a directed arc with fractional LP usage f, the children enforce flow atmost floor(f) or at least ceil(f). Route coefficients count traversals ofthe arc; branch duals also reach pricing through that arc. BranchConstraint::ArcFlow::arc takes the arc's position inproblem.graph.arcs, while Route::arcs stores public arc IDs. UseRootProblem::arc_position(id) to convert an ID to a position.

title: Routing branching
heading: Strong branching and diving
text: Strong branching and diving Strong branching is enabled by default. Its three phases retain up to 100restricted-LP candidates, price three survivors heuristically, then evaluateone with exact pricing. StrongBranchingOptions exposes the phase and timebudgets. Disable it with --no-strong-branching. Strong round-up diving uses isolated route-fixing trials and depth,discrepancy, node, and time limits. Disable it with --no-diving.Heuristic trial objectives and dive bounds cannot certify the original node.See Tree lifecycle for bound and incumbent handling.

title: Routing cuts
heading: Route-load knapsack and resource IDs
text: Route-load knapsack and resource IDs KnapsackCutConfig::new(rows) takes integer resource rows fromcuts::knapsack::KnapsackRow. Separation uses route resource loads, andpricing must charge the same load-dependent contribution. Ordinary arc-onlycosts are insufficient for this family. KnapsackCutConfig::with_resource_indices(map) maps resource IDs in thoserows to coordinates in the pricing solver. An empty map uses identitymapping. For example, an input resource identified as 7 can map to solvercoordinate 1. This changes the coordinate lookup, while preserving resourceIDs in the cut associations. The mapping must remain valid through pricing,enumeration, and child inheritance. Keep rows integer-scaled according to their model semantics. The resourcemap is not a unit conversion. See the mapped-resource and load-dependentpricing cases in the integration tests forcomplete fixtures.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Enumeration gate
text: Enumeration gate The route universe must be complete and its route count must not exceed theconfigured threshold. Equality and a completed empty universe are accepted.BALDESmaxNumOfEnumSolutionsForMIP defaults to 10,000;BALDESmaxNumOfEnumSolsForEndOfNodeMIP defaults to zero and is raised to at leastthe normal threshold. An incomplete universe never passes the gate. Settingonly the end-of-node option to zero does not disable the solve, because the normal threshold stillraises it. The gate counts retained enumerated routes before adding anypreviously priced elementary witness routes to the integer model.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Preserving node semantics
text: Preserving node semantics The snapshot adapter copies the current physical row order, including baserows, inherited typed branches, and every active capacity, rank-one, strongk-path and route-load knapsack row. It rebuilds route columns using currentbase/branch coefficients and full-memory cut coefficients. It preservesexisting route upper bounds, including zero bounds. Artificial columns areomitted, so finite artificial penalties cannot masquerade as feasibility. Previously priced elementary routes are independently reconstructed andvalidated before being retained as possible witnesses. Enumeration can haveremoved a previously found incumbent route at its cutoff; retaining validatedold routes avoids losing that witness. Every added route still receives everybranch and active cut row. EnumeratedMipOutput::coverage_cutoff records the incumbent under which theuniverse was restricted (or the existing 1e12 fallback). A proof about thismatrix alone cannot exclude solutions above that cutoff. The tree uses at mostthe minimum of the proved MIP bound and that coverage cutoff. It records avalidated routing witness before closing a gap. Without a witness, a finitecoverage cutoff cannot establish global infeasibility. For snapshots with fixed partial routes,the integer model uses residual row bounds and a fixed objective offset. Returnedbounds and objectives include that offset, and route_values includes the fixedroutes when a witness is available, including a completed empty remainder.

title: Enumerated node MIP with HiGHS
heading: Outcomes
text: Outcomes Outcome Interpretation Optimal HiGHS proved the integer model optimal and supplied a validated improving witness Infeasible HiGHS proved the transferred integer model infeasible; node interpretation still depends on enumeration coverage ObjectiveCutoff The proved integer optimum does not improve the caller's cutoff; no feasible incumbent is invented from that cutoff TimeLimit / NodeLimit Unfinished solve; any validated improving incumbent is retained, but the tree does not treat the limit as a proof Incomplete Other or ambiguous statuses, including unbounded-or-infeasible and unusable witnesses; no node-closing proof A finite objective_cutoff filters improving witnesses after solving; it isnot installed as a HiGHS search cutoff. The source model is copied beforesolving, so a supplied cutoff never substitutes for a feasible incumbent.Coefficients with nonzero magnitude at most 1e-12 are rejected to avoidsilent matrix changes in HiGHS. HiGHS relative and absolute MIP gaps are set to zero. Its model status isretained in MipOutput::solver_status, with solution, dual bound, node count,simplex iterations, and elapsed time. Tree JSON adds enumerated_mip_calls andenumerated_mip_nodes; its existing mip_nodes includes this work too.

title: BALDES pricing options
heading: HGS initial columns and master backends
text:
HGS initial columns and master backends Run HGS for a separate, positive search budget before solving the root or tree: cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- \
  cvrp instances/cvrplib/E-n22-k4.vrp --hgs-time 10 --hgs-columns all --tree
 --hgs-columns best (default) inserts routes from the best feasible HGS solution.all retains distinct routes seen during population insertion, including thoselater discarded or lost at a restart. A positive integer such as--hgs-columns 100 inserts up to 100 cheapest new feasible routes, ranked byoriginal arc-cost sum, with arc IDs breaking ties. Validation and deduplicationhappen before ranking; routes already supplied as initial columns do not consumethis quota.If fewer routes are available, all available routes are inserted. This rankinguses route cost, not reduced cost or whole-solution quality. Every candidateis replayed against the actual graph, using its resource bounds and arc costs;HGS's integer demands do not establish original-model feasibility. HGS uses theinstance's distance convention, with full-precision unrounded distances forSolomon instances by default. --rounding tenth explicitly enables truncatedtenths in both HGS and the target graph; --rounding none keeps unroundeddistances. Explicit distance matrices retain their supplied precision. A complete best plansupplies an incumbent only after original-model validation. --seed controlsthe random seed. HGS runs before the solver's --time budget starts; its searchlimit is cooperative, checked between HGS operations. Keeping all encounteredroutes uses more memory than keeping only the best plan. Select native IPM for restricted-master solves with --master ipm. Thisselection automatically disables dual stabilization, including at descendantnodes. The default remains --master clp. IPM solves are rebuilt from thecurrent sparse matrix and return their own primal values, duals, and reducedcosts. Clp still stores the mutable model and snapshots, so the routing drivercontinues to require the clp build feature. Basis-dependent cut retirement isskipped for IPM; it has no simplex basis. The separate conservative-boundcertificate routine retains its bounded auxiliary Clp solve. IPM time limits are cooperative,checked between Newton iterations; a factorization may exceed the remainingbudget before control returns. Numerical failures are reported as errors. During column generation, IPM uses the bound-driven accuracy rule fromMunari and Gondzio (2013), Section 3.1, Algorithm 1(Munari and Gondzio (2013), p. 2029). It starts with epsilon = 0.5, thenuses epsilon = min(1, gap / 10) with a numerical floor of 1e-9, wheregap = max(0, UB - LB) / (1 + abs(UB)). UB is the best artificial-freerestricted-master primal objective; LB comes only from exact LP pricing.Integer incumbents, heuristic pricing estimates, and stronger integer-domaincertificates do not control IPM accuracy. New cuts reset these accuracy bounds.Only the optimality gap is relaxed; primal and dual feasibility remain at1e-9. Exhausted pricing triggers an accurate master solve and another pricingcheck before separation or completion. Standalone master solves and strongbranching retain accurate solves. The requested tolerance is available asmaster_gap_tolerance in Rust's column-generation iteration history. This implements the paper's adaptive master accuracy. IPM still rebuilds eachrestricted master; the stored-interior-iterate warm starts in Section 3.4 andearly cut generation in Algorithm 2 are not implemented by this option. Select HiGHS for restricted-master LP solves with --master highs: cargo build --release --features clp,highs
./target/release/baldes vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 25 --master highs --log
 HiGHS preserves the requested stabilization setting; use --no-stabilizationto turn it off. The native HiGHS instance persists across LP solves. Row/columninsertion, cost and coefficient edits, RHS/bound changes, and cleanup updatethat instance directly, retaining its basis and reusable simplex state. Theadapter also reuses solution buffers, batches row/column insertion, and servesan unchanged optimal LP from its cache without another native solve. Node forks copy the sparse matrix in bulk and install the source's currentnative basis into an independent HiGHS instance. A child refactorizes its ownbasis once; siblings never share mutable solver state. Solutions, reduced costs,and cut-cleanup basis statuses come from HiGHS. A failed mirrored edit discardsthe cached backend, so a later solve reconstructs it from the canonical modelrather than using a partially synchronized instance.Clp remains the matrix/snapshot store and the backend for the separate boundedcertificate auxiliary LP. Selecting HiGHS without the highs build featurereturns an explicit error. Enable HiGHS in make config when building with Make. Python accepts master_solver="highs"; build its extension with the highsfeature (for example, maturin develop --release --features highs).pybaldes.has_highs reports whether that build feature is available. In Rust, set RootOptions::master_solver to MasterSolver::Highs orMasterSolver::Ipm. For HGS seeding,call instance.seed_hgs(&problem, rounding, &mut options, &HgsWarmStart { ... })before passing those options to root::solve or TreeOptions::root. The typesHgsWarmStart and HgsColumns::{Best, All, Top(n)} are exported by baldes::inputs.The returned summary reports inserted/rejected columns and any validatedincumbent. Existing initial columns are retained and duplicates are skipped. Python exposes the same root options: result = pybaldes.solve_root(
    "instances/cvrplib/E-n22-k4.vrp", problem_type="cvrp",
    hgs_time=10.0, hgs_columns=100, hgs_seed=7, master_solver="ipm",
)

title: BALDES pricing options
heading: Terminal progress
text:
Terminal progress Routing solves are quiet by default. --verbose, -v, or --log enables analigned column-generation table on stderr. It prints iteration 1, every tenthiteration, and the final state, followed by the CG status and work totals.--log-interval N enables the same log with a positive custom interval.The interval applies to each CG solve, including descendant nodes and treetrials. Each node reports its depth, master algorithm, and stabilization mode. ./target/release/baldes vrptw instances/R101.txt --customers 25 \
  --hgs-time 2 --hgs-columns 100 --master ipm --verbose
 RMP obj is the restricted-master objective and may include artificial columns;it is not a feasible routing objective or a global lower bound. Lower boundis the separately certified bound. Incumbent is the current objective upperbound; a caller-supplied root upper bound still carries its feasibilityassumption. Gap % is 100 * max(0, incumbent - bound) / max(1, abs(incumbent)).Unknown or nonfinite values appear as --. Min RC is the latest pricingminimum, +Cols counts inserted columns in that iteration, Cols is the currentmaster size including artificials, and Phase is the pricing phase. Time iselapsed wall time within the current CG call. A CG Optimal status does notby itself certify an integer routing optimum. The logger adds no color escapes or cursor control, so redirected logs remainreadable. stdout summaries and --json files retain their result formats.Standalone hgs --verbose uses the same HGS progress table; during warm starts,that table and its summary appear before the column-generation log. Rust callers set options.cg.log_interval = Some(10) (or the generic CGOptions::log_interval). Python callers use verbose=True, log_interval=10.Python's interval defaults to 10 and must be positive; verbose=False keepsCG silent.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Dual-price stabilization
text: Dual-price stabilization Documentation index · Tree lifecycle Column generation can repeatedly produce similar master duals and columns.BALDES optionally smooths the dual point sent to pricing, using a storedcenter and bounded retries when smoothed pricing finds no fresh columns.It is enabled by default in column_generation::Options. The implementation isDualPriceSmoothing, integrated by thecolumn-generation loop. The sections belowdescribe the implemented update and retry rules.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Smoothing weight
text:
Smoothing weight For raw master duals raw, stored center, and an outward point outward: pricing[i] = (1 - effective_alpha) * outward[i]
           + effective_alpha * center[i]
 By default outward = raw. Larger alpha means more weight on the center.At alpha zero pricing uses the outward point; at alpha one it uses the center.Reducing alpha moves pricing back toward the current master duals. After interpolation, a positive dual on a LessEqual row or a negative dualon a GreaterEqual row is set to zero when its magnitude exceeds theconfigured tolerance. Equality rows have no such sign restriction.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Parameters
text: Parameters These are Rust master::stabilization::Parameters, configured throughRootOptions::cg.smoothing or directly in column_generation::Options.They are separate from the named BALDES pricing options. Parameter Default Behavior alpha_factor 1.0 Below 1: use that base alpha and the linear retry rule; otherwise adapt alpha dynamically initial_alpha 0.5 Initial base alpha for the dynamic mode beta_factor 0.0 Zero: use raw outward point; positive: enable the directional construction below max_updates 10 Maximum smoothed retry updates before returning to raw duals min_gap 0.0 Minimum accepted gap, using the comparison tolerance max_gap 0.0 Maximum accepted gap; nonpositive disables the upper gate minimum_stage 0 Minimum stage accepted by after_master tolerance 1e-6 General comparison and sign-correction tolerance The reference stores alpha_factor, beta_factor, min_gap and max_gapas single-precision controls. The constructor rounds these fields through f32before using them as f64. A factor that rounds to zero disables stabilization. The column-generation caller passes the current pricing stage. Its gap comparesthe inherited node lower bound with the best artificial-free restricted-LPobjective accepted before this solve, using the reference comparison tolerance.It tracks these separately from the global integer incumbent. A new cut orenumeration round carries the certified lower bound and resets the LP bound.Unknown bounds use finite -1e12/+1e12 sentinels; a known lower bound with anunknown LP bound therefore gives a gap slightly below one. Warm starts retainthe parent certificate.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Lifecycle
text: Lifecycle Method Effect restart_schedule(phase) Reset base/effective alpha, retry count, active flag, and center phase; retain the stored center/bound vectors after_master(...) Apply a pending center, store raw duals/senses, reset retries, and activate smoothing if the stage/gap/alpha gates allow it after_pricing(feedback) Consider a center update, adjust base alpha, and decide whether pricing should retry after_iteration() Clear the moved-center marker and return active pricing to raw duals remap_rows(map) Compact dual, center, sense, and pending-center vectors after row removal The first master iteration uses raw duals. Cut/enumeration transitions restartthe schedule; row cleanup applies the row map. Removing columns alone doesnot change row coordinates and does not require a center remap.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Pricing retries and alpha updates
text:
Pricing retries and alpha updates Feedback includes the fresh negative-column count, a subgradient vector,Lagrangian value, and pricing phase. In the column-generation driver, thesubgradient starts at the row RHS and subtracts multiplicity times the bestreturned acceptable column's coefficients. A near-zero or rounded-zero reducedcost does not suppress this contribution. On the first pricing pass in dynamic mode (alpha_factor >= 1): if no fresh negative columns or angle > 1e-12:
    alpha -= 0.1
else if angle < -1e-12 and alpha is below the near-one gate:
    alpha += 0.1 * (1 - alpha)
 The angle threshold is 1e-12, independently of Parameters::tolerance.The near-one gate includes the general tolerance and a relative margin.Updating base alpha affects subsequent master iterations; retries update thecurrent effective alpha separately. The angle is calculated only on that firstadaptive pricing pass and retained during subsequent mispricing retries. If fresh negative columns exist, or smoothing is inactive, after_pricingreturns false and stops retrying. Otherwise it increments misprices and uses: dynamic mode: effective_alpha = 1 - 2 * (1 - effective_alpha)
fixed-base mode: effective_alpha = 1 - misprices * (1 - alpha)
 It republishes a smoothed point only while the retry count is at mostmax_updates and effective alpha exceeds the tolerance. When either gatefails, it deactivates smoothing and requests a final retry at raw duals.“Fixed” describes the base alpha, not an unchanging effective retry weight.The dynamic formula preserves the compiled reference's floating-point operationorder; rewriting it as 2 * effective_alpha - 1 can change the result.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Center updates
text:
Center updates A nonfinite Lagrangian value is ignored. If the current center phase is lessthan or equal to the feedback phase, a finite center bound is replaced onlywhen the new value improves it beyond tolerance. A lower-numbered feedbackphase can reset the center phase and accept a different bound without thatsame improvement requirement. The accepted pricing point and feedback subgradient become a pendingcenter, installed by the next after_master call. Consequently the storedcenter bound is not unconditionally monotone across phase changes. The angle helper computes: toward = pricing - center
angle = dot(toward, feedback_subgradient)
      / (norm(toward) * norm(feedback_subgradient))
 The division is unguarded. A zero denominator may yield NaN; comparisonswith it then fail. This behavior differs from forcing an angle of zero.

title: Dual-price stabilization
heading: Optional directional construction
text:
Optional directional construction With positive beta_factor, let d = raw - center, l = norm(d), and gbe the stored normalized center subgradient. A negligible l returns raw duals.For beta_factor == 1, beta is the cosine between d and g; a negligiblesubgradient also returns raw duals. Otherwise the configured beta is used.Beta is clamped to [0, 1] before constructing: outward = center + (1 - beta) * d + beta * l * g
 A negligible subgradient contributes zero to its directional term. When theconstructed step has norm above 1e-12, it is rescaled to length l. Thischanges the outward point before the alpha interpolation. Mispricing retries usethe raw outward point. Restart invalidates the automatic direction until a subsequent accepted centerprovides a new normalized subgradient. Retaining the old vector alone does notmake it valid. The 54-case parameter corpus covers this capacity-row transition.

text: Cuts cuts/mod.rs exports the registry and its public types. capacity/, knapsack/,kpath/, and rank_one/ own their respective cut families. shared/ owns commoncut-state, graph, and container helpers. Compatibility exports retainpaths such as cuts::state and cuts::separation.

title: Source layout
heading: Master and tree
text: Master and tree master/root/mod.rs owns solved-node snapshots, mutable root state, and solveor inheritance entry points. problem.rs owns rows and route coefficients;options.rs owns root and cut-family configuration; controller.rs ownscolumn-generation callbacks and separation scheduling. master/root/incumbent.rs validates integerroute quantities, exact original row activities and scalar resource feasibility,then evaluates an objective upper bound from original arc costs. Physical arcchains determine the resource checks; recorded nodes must agree with them. master/root/domain.rs validates unit visit-countcover rows, fixed-route residuals and disposable scalar resources beforecollecting a CanonicalCoverRelaxation. This projects feasible integer routesonto canonical physical paths; it does not establish completeness of an NG LPor authorize cut rows or root bound publication.ConservativeCoverRelaxation uses downward resource bounds to cover exact-realfeasible paths, including arithmetic boundaries missed by strict forward replay.Its states describe a relaxation and cannot serve as integer route witnesses. master/root/certificate.rs publishes rootbounds for eligible unit-cover models. It restores conservative physical paths,proves optional rows over residual integer partitions, obtains auxiliary LPduals, and checks them against raw original costs and coefficients with directedarithmetic. Unsupported models or exhausted budgets return an unknown bound.Auxiliary slacks supply duals but never enter the certified matrix. master/root/restoration.rs recovers bounded,validated original columns when exhausted pricing leaves positive artificials.It replays physical paths, exact resources and vertex elementarity beforeregistration; generic CG then re-solves rather than inferring infeasibility. master/root/cover_rows.rs computes exactinteger row-activity ranges over residual customer partitions of that domain.It relaxes fleet and branch restrictions and has explicit state, work and timelimits. Passing its range test proves a row valid on those canonical covers;resource-schedule projection and original-domain eligibility remain separate.Its additive-weight upper proof checks every auxiliary path and uses exactinteger cover conservation to validate weighted packing rows without subset DP. master/tree/mod.rs owns node processing and the search queue. Its siblingcandidates.rs, strong.rs, and diving.rs own candidate generation, strongbranching, and diving. Typed constraints live in master/branching.rs.LP backends remain under master/solvers/. Shared integer result types are inmaster/solvers/mip.rs; master/solvers/highs/integer.rs transfers completemodels to HiGHS. master/root/integer.rs prepares complete enumerated masters;master/tree/integer.rs runs the optional end-of-node solve. master/networks.rs coordinates fresh roots withmultiple independent pricing graphs and shared master rows.master/network_bounds.rs supplies conservativegraph-walk bound certificates. See multiple networks for thecoefficient mapping and current integration limits. master/certificates.rs evaluates conservativelower bounds for explicit finite matrices using original cost terms and averified total-column-quantity row. It shares directed arithmetic with networkbounds through master/rounding.rs. A finite-matrix bound applies to an originalrouting domain only after column completeness or excluded-domain coverage androw validity have been established separately. Public paths remain master::root::{RootProblem, RootOptions, NodeSnapshot}and master::tree::{TreeOptions, BranchingOptions}.

title: Source layout
heading: Pricing and enumeration
text: Pricing and enumeration pricing/mod.rs owns Solver, construction and forks, options, engine and cutpreparation, and column-generation round updates. solve.rs runs pricing phases;universe.rs manages enumeration, inspection, and direct fixing;completion.rs completes labels and restores arcs;fixing_workflow.rs dispatches native fixing/enumeration modes;variable_costs.rs handles variable costs, route-value corrections and rawfunctor repricing. A rounded winning route alone cannot certify the raw minimum:the functor uses an independent raw-cost pricing domain, preserving logicalbranch constraints and sharing the call's time budget. Heuristic phases leavethe lower bound unknown;relaxation.rs manages dynamic NG updates and route validation.branching.rs, phases.rs, fixing.rs, and controller.rs provide supportingresources, phase definitions, fixing result types, and round state. If a backward candidate cannot be replayed within forward resource windows,pricing/solve.rs rebuilds a forward-only search under the remaining calldeadline, reloading cuts, branch resources and explicit physical exclusions.This recovers the minimum even when the failed candidate displaced valid pathsfrom the bounded solution pool. Route.resource_profile records the source state and the state after every arc.Label reconstruction preserves waiting from bucket jumps instead of replacingit with earliest arrival. Root column identities include these schedules, soequal arc paths with different resource states remain distinct. Code constructingRoute literals must supply the profile; resources is its final state. enumeration/mod.rs exports Controls, Enumeration, Label, CutTables,Storage, Path, and PathStorage. Their implementation files arecontrols.rs, engine.rs, label.rs, storage.rs, and paths.rs. enumeration/domain.rs exportsCompleteCanonicalPaths, a bounded collector of physical vertex-simple pathsunder canonical forward scalar-resource extension. It preserves parallel arcidentity and borrows the graph. Budget exhaustion discards the partial result.It keeps one earliest resource profile per path; callers must establish anyequivalence to all routing columns or alternative schedules separately. CompleteResourceRelaxation shares the bounded physical-path search whileusing directed additions for disposable resources. Its RelaxedResourcePathvalues provide resource lower bounds; extra infeasible paths may remain.Unsupported resource kinds and arithmetic failures return an explicit failure.

title: Source layout
heading: C API and instances
text: C API and instances C API implementation modules are private; public functions and ABI types arere-exported through api. Shared handle validation and error handling stay inapi/mod.rs. Symbol names and calling conventions are unchanged. inputs/mod.rs owns Customer, Instance, and Rounding; parsing.rs readsinstances; graph.rs builds pricing graphs; root.rs provides the optional Clpadapter. The public path is inputs::Instance. Standalone network, root checkpoint, labeling profile, and arena test moduleslive in the sibling baldes-verification/overlays/unit/ directory. Its runnerattaches them to an isolated source snapshot; production builds need no external files. For new code, place routines with the component that owns their state and addexports at its existing facade when needed. Keep numerical and branchingbehavior changes separate from file organization so each diff remainsreviewable. enumeration/frontier.rs records cached candidatecosts rejected during enumeration, ordered join breaks, and completion rejections.These are observations from that run's cost epoch, preserved by pricing forks;retained-path repricing does not update them. Representative pruning and symmetriccost transformations are marked explicitly. The observations alone do not certifyan original-domain lower bound or account for a previously restricted bucket grid.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Website and documentation publishing
text: Website and documentation publishing Documentation index · Build and validation The website consists of the handwritten landing page in landing/ and HTMLguides compiled from docs/**/*.md. Markdown files are the documentation source;do not edit generated landing/docs/ files.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Compile and preview
text:
Compile and preview The website build needs Python 3.10 or newer. It does not build the Rust solver.Create a separate environment and install the pinned documentation dependencies: python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r .github/scripts/docs-requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python .github/scripts/compile_docs.py
.venv/bin/python -m http.server 8000 --directory landing
 Open http://localhost:8000/ for the landing page andhttp://localhost:8000/docs/ for the guides. Use an HTTP server rather thanopening HTML files directly, so search can load its local index. On Windows, use .venv/Scripts/python.exe instead of the bin/pythonpath. Re-run the compiler after changing Markdown, reader styles, or scripts.No JavaScript bundler or external search service is required.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: What the compiler does
text: What the compiler does Compiles README.md to index.html and other Markdown files to matching.html paths, including nested directories. Builds sidebar navigation from this documentation index's link order,followed by any additional guides. Renders tables, fenced code with syntax highlighting, heading anchors, anon-page contents list, and previous/next guide links. Rewrites local Markdown links to generated HTML, validates local links andheading fragments, and maps repository source links to GitHub. Copies linked local images and writes a section-level search index. Escapes embedded HTML in Markdown. The shared page templates supply thesite's markup; guide authors use Markdown for content. Replaces only marked generated output after rendering succeeds, removingstale generated pages. A failed build leaves the previous output intact. A new guide appears in the reader automatically. Add its link tothe documentation index to choose its navigation position.README.md and index.md in the same directory would both produceindex.html; the compiler rejects that collision.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Custom destinations
text:
Custom destinations .venv/bin/python .github/scripts/compile_docs.py \
  --output /tmp/baldes-docs \
  --base-url https://example.org/baldes/ \
  --repository-url https://github.com/lseman/baldes
 --source defaults to the repository's docs/ directory. --output defaultsto landing/docs/. Source and output must be separate directories, neitherinside the other. Local repository links must resolve within the repository.The output includes its own styles and scripts; the Home link expects thelanding page one level above the documentation root. Internal links and assets are relative, so the website works both at / andunder a project prefix such as /baldes/. --base-url controls canonicalpage URLs; it does not change internal navigation.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Automated publishing
text: Automated publishing The Pages workflow runs on pushes tomain that change the landing page, documentation, compiler, or its tests anddependencies. It installs Python dependencies, runs compiler tests, compilesthe guides, and publishes landing/ to the gh-pages branch. It also supportsmanual dispatch. Deployment replaces the published file tree so deleted guides do not remainon the website. Generated output is ignored by Git; commit the Markdown,compiler, templates/assets, and dependency file instead. Editing files locallydoes not publish them until the workflow runs after a push.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Reader accessibility
text: Reader accessibility The page templates use headings, landmarks, and visible form labels to exposestructure (WCAG 1.3.1). Skip links bypass repeated navigation (2.4.1), andinteractive elements have visible keyboard focus (2.4.7). The capacity controluses a native labeled range input, while search and copy actions announcestatus changes (4.1.2 / 4.1.3). Reduced-motion preferences disable smoothscrolling and decorative transitions.

title: Website and documentation publishing
heading: Validate changes
text:
Validate changes .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_compile_docs.py'
.venv/bin/python .github/scripts/compile_docs.py
 The tests cover nested navigation, local/source/image links, duplicate anchors,tables, code escaping/highlighting, search entries, destination collisions,output protection, and rebuilds. For visual changes, also inspect a narrowviewport, keyboard focus, search results, code-copy buttons, and the landingpage's capacity illustration. The illustration groups customers into routes;it does not execute the Rust solver or claim optimal routes.

title: Root benchmarks
heading: Root benchmarks
text: Root benchmarks Documentation index · Build and validation Root relaxations of Solomon VRPTW instances (100 customers). Both solversuse the same split-depot graph with unroundedEuclidean distances, the same NG neighbourhoods (the 8 nearest customers), theClp master and no reduced-cost fixing or enumeration. Times are the solvers' ownroot timers, medians of three runs, each solver running alone on an AMDRyzen 9 9950X. The reference run uses one thread; BALDES runs the forward and backwardlabeling of exact pricing on two threads, so it is timed on one and two cores. Root relaxation solve times On C101–C103, C201, C202 and R102, rank-one separation finds no violated cut,so those runs equal the ones without cuts.

title: Root benchmarks
heading: Original-domain certificate search regression
text: Original-domain certificate search regression An October 19, 2026 rerun found a regression introduced with conservativeoriginal-domain certificates in commit 9631e9d. Every exact pricing call couldrepeat a bounded search of the same immutable path domain. On C202, temporaryinstrumentation measured 90 unsuccessful certificate attempts consuming 13.30 sof a 26.56 s root solve. The collector scanned the entire graph's arc list ateach DFS frame and polled the clock for every scan. The collector now builds ordered outgoing arc lists and polls its cooperativedeadline in batches of at most 64 work units, with explicit validation andcompletion checks. A cache scoped to one root/node solve remembers deterministicdomain failures at their work, path and storage limits. New duals or cuts cannotcomplete that same domain within smaller limits. Larger limits may retry;deadline and allocation failures are retried. Child solves start fresh caches.An incomplete search still supplies no certificate. The same 13 workloads above were run sequentially on the same Ryzen 9 9950X,with Clp, reference-compatible NG size 8, unrounded distances, enumerationdisabled, default stabilization, release optimization level 3 and thin LTO.One warm-up precedes three measured runs per workload/core configuration.Two-core medians, in seconds: Workload Regressed build Fixed build Original chart C101 0.368 0.068 0.057 C202 25.722 12.463 12.160 R101 0.358 0.054 0.045 R201, rank-one enabled 15.597 7.987 7.270 Geometric mean, all 13 2.276 0.842 0.786 This fixes the main regression: the two-core geometric mean improves by 2.70×,removing about 96% of the added time relative to the rounded chart values.The fixed build remains about 7% above the chart overall; these measurementsdo not establish identical performance to the older binary. Each of the 104fixed-build runs finishes with root CG status Optimal, and every non-timingJSON field matches the corresponding pre-fix workload, including full history,routes, objectives, cuts, iterations and pricing calls. Local scripts, frozen binaries, source patch, individual outputs, profiles andvalidation logs are retained in results/root-speed-fix-20261019/; the pre-fixsuite is in results/root-rerun-20261019/. These are ignored local artifacts.

title: Root benchmarks
heading: Numerical and certified bound modes
text: Numerical and certified bound modes Normal root and tree solves now default to numerical bounds and skip the fullcertificate transaction. --bound-mode certified selects independent boundvalidation, attempted at closing pricing passes or when the master objectivesuggests the incumbent gap can close. Results label the selected mode and keepnumerical estimates separate from certificates; unsuccessful validation leavesthe certified bound unknown. An October 19 rerun used the same 13 chart workloads, Clp and two physical coreson the same Ryzen 9 9950X. Trials alternated modes sequentially, with one warm-upand three measured runs per case/mode. The numerical flag was omitted to verifythe default. The geometric mean of case medians was 0.834 s in numerical modeand 0.842 s in certified mode. The times are close after the earlier failed-searchcache fix; this change primarily makes computation and bound guarantees explicit. All 104 runs finish with root CG status Optimal. Every JSON field excepttimers and bound metadata matches the preceding certificate-cache build,including LP objectives, full histories, routes, cuts and pricing counts.All 13 certified-mode workloads retain unknown certified bounds within theirsearch limits: these times do not measure successful large-instance proofs.Separate small-instance tests cover successful certification, failure withoutnumerical fallback, both tree modes, and mode changes through node snapshots.Raw results, the frozen binary, source patch and scripts are retained locally inresults/bound-modes-20261019/.

title: Root benchmarks
heading: HiGHS master reuse
text: HiGHS master reuse Local measurement on October 19, 2026: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, Rust 1.97.1,HiGHS 1.15.1, release optimization level 3 and thin LTO. HiGHS uses its defaultthread settings. Trials run sequentially; these numbers describe this machineand workload, not a general speed guarantee. A fixed growing-LP workload starts with 120 unit-cover rows and singletoncolumns, then inserts 30 batches of 30 three-row columns. It compares persistentHiGHS state with explicitly discarding the HiGHS cache before each batch. Bothmodes retain the same canonical model and receive the same columns. The timercovers batch construction, insertion, and solving. Five alternating pairs followone untimed warm-up per mode. All 150 compared objectives agree within 1e-7. Fixed LP workload Median time Forced cold rebuild 110.2 ms Persistent model and basis 63.1 ms This workload is 1.75× faster with reuse. Regression tests also verifyzero simplex pivots for an unchanged LP, installation of the parent basis inan independent fork, and agreement with cold solves after edits and cleanup. End-to-end CLI comparisons use the pre-optimization release binary and theoptimized release binary, each with --master highs --rank1 --no-enumeration --time 15, default stabilization, and five alternating pairs per customercount. The table reports median process wall time: Root workload Before After Speedup R101, 10 customers 34.0 ms 27.3 ms 1.25× R101, 25 customers 27.0 ms 11.4 ms 2.36× R101, 50 customers 464.1 ms 276.2 ms 1.68× All runs finish with root CG status Optimal, and paired LP objectives agreewithin 1e-7. Warm bases change duals and pricing trajectories, so these rootspeedups include changes in pricing work and are not isolated LP timings.They do not establish integer routing optimality or full solver parity. Reproducible benchmark source, raw timings, and frozen binaries are kept outsidethe repository in the local ../baldes-verification/benchmarks/highs-warm-start/workbench. The production repository contains only these measurement notes.

title: Root benchmarks
heading: HiGHS simplex direction
text: HiGHS simplex direction A second October 19, 2026 measurement on the same machine and HiGHS 1.15.1compares the persistent master with HiGHS's default dual simplex strategy (1)and adaptive simplex selection (0). The adapter now selects 0: new columnspreserve primal feasibility while cuts and bound changes can instead favor dualsimplex. Both modes retain the native model and basis, use the same 1e-7primal/dual tolerances, and retain the single cold restart on a numerical failure.Scaling, pivot pricing, factorization-update limits and column bounds are unchanged. Eleven configurations were screened on R201/100, including forced primal,Devex/Dantzig/steepest-edge pricing, scaling disabled, and shorter factorizationupdate limits. Adaptive selection provided the measured improvement withoutforcing primal simplex for cut and branch edits. Forced dual Devex and Dantzigwere slower; the tested scaling/update-limit changes did not improve this case. Three alternating, sequential before/after pairs per workload used one frozenrelease executable and a native option/profiling shim. No builds ran during themeasurements. Times below are median process wall times; iterations are outercolumn-generation master solves, distinct from simplex pivots. Root workload Dual time Adaptive time Dual CG iterations Adaptive CG iterations R201, 100 customers 5.812 s 3.504 s 477 356 R101, 50 customers 0.283 s 0.288 s 33 31 R101, 50 customers, rank-one enabled 0.285 s 0.284 s 33 31 R101, 10 customers, rank-one enabled 0.029 s 0.027 s 14 14 C101, 100 customers 0.421 s 0.367 s 96 35 All 30 valid runs finish with CG status Optimal, and paired root LP objectivesagree within 1e-7. R201 simplex pivots fall from 36,816 to 21,953 and measurednative LP time from 2.905 s to 1.188 s; the numerical restart count falls fromone to zero. These are workload-specific measurements of root LP optimization,not integer routing optimality or a guarantee of identical Clp/HiGHS trajectories.An attempted RC201 workload was excluded because its input file is absent.Raw commands, timings, counters, option shim and frozen executable are retainedin ../baldes-verification/benchmarks/highs-tuning-20261019/.
