title: Build and validation
heading: What the checks establish
text: What the checks establish Small integer tests compare against exhaustive route or variable enumeration.Lifecycle tests verify parent/sibling isolation and inherited branch/cut rows.MIP tests distinguish feasible witnesses from proof outcomes and check thatlimits do not certify an unfinished node. Column-generation tests also check artificial-penalty exhaustion. Exact pricingwith positive artificials proves optimality only for the penalized master;exhausting the penalty-update budget returns Stalled. It does not prove theoriginal model infeasible. Increasing that budget can recover a feasible realsolution, but callers must still inspect status and solution feasibility. Root incumbent checks round approximately integral route quantities, validatethe resulting logical row activities, and evaluate an upper bound from originalarc costs. The numerical LP objective alone is not accepted as an integerincumbent. Arithmetic overflow leaves the candidate unaccepted.Scalar resource checks accumulate original consumptions exactly, apply disposablewaiting or equality semantics, and compare exact states with vertex/arc windows.They also recheck fixed routes and match recorded nodes to the physical arcchain. Stored floating resource profiles do not prove witness feasibility. CG passes its remaining wall-time budget to both Clp and HiGHS throughLpMaster::solve_with_time_limit. Root preparation, CG and pricing share thesame root deadline. Auxiliary Clp callers can also use solve_limited with anexplicit iteration budget. Limits are cooperative and scoped to the call;previous backend limits are restored. Typed stop outcomes are distinct from LPinfeasibility, and cached arrays from a stopped call do not authorize a newsolution or certificate. Custom LP backends must override the compatibilitymethod to enforce their own in-solve deadline. Finite-matrix certificate tests cover fractional quantities, invalid dual signs,original cost cancellation, fixed objective terms and unproved multiplicityrows. Unsupported or overflowing arithmetic returns an unknown bound. Thesechecks do not establish completeness of a routing column universe. In explicit certified mode (RootOptions::bound_mode = BoundMode::Certified),the root controller combines conservative disposable-resource path coverage,residual cover-row proofs and finite-matrix numerical bounds before publishinga lower certificate. The transaction shares the root deadline, with anadditional 250 ms cap, ten million logical work units, 10,000 paths and one millionstored arc/coefficient positions. Row DP has at most 65,536 states and theauxiliary LP has at most 10,000 iterations. Limits are cooperative rather thanhard heap/CPU caps. Failure leaves the bound unknown; the ordinary pricingestimate is not substituted. Node tests cover interruption, omission ofunproved rows and parent-model isolation. General resource kinds and arbitraryfractional fixed-row shifts remain unsupported by this certificate. Numerical mode is the default and skips that certificate transaction. It keepsexact pricing and route-feasibility checks, and labels its bounds as numerical.Tests verify that numerical mode never invokes certification, unknowncertificates cannot authorize strict pruning, and warm starts preserve boundprovenance when changing modes. Certified mode attempts proof at closing exactpasses or when the current master objective suggests the incumbent gap canclose, rather than on every improving exact batch. Weighted packing rows can use an exact additive envelope instead of partitionDP: every path must satisfy denominator * coefficient <= customer weight sum.An integer residual cover then has row activity at most the floor of its totalremaining weight divided by the denominator. The proof checks actual pathcoefficients, signed weights, fixed residual covers and interruption. Otherrows retain the general partition audit. Sparse row extraction avoids scanningthe entire matrix once per cut. CG keeps its LP pricing convergence estimate separate from the publishedinteger-domain certificate, including for warm starts. A bound on integersolutions can exceed the pricing LP optimum. The independent fractional-coverregression checks that such a bound does not skip improving LP columns. If exact pricing exhausts the allowed artificial penalties, the routingcontroller can restore bounded original columns before returning Stalled.Each candidate passes physical, exact-resource and vertex-elementarity replay;relaxation resource bounds are not route witnesses. Recovery adds columns andre-solves the master before accepting its point. Incomplete recovery leaves thenode unknown. Arc-element descriptors currently decline this optional recovery.Normal regressions cover a large-cost routing case, exhausted penalties,ineligible columns and deadline interruption without route-cache mutation. A finite caller-supplied RootOptions::incumbent is an assumed upper bound.Its scalar value is not a validated route witness; callers must supply aconservative upper bound on the original objective. Automatically discoveredincumbents use the exact checks described above. Canonical path collector unit tests cover cycles, parallel arcs, waiting,equality resources, direct terminal arcs, malformed input and exact budgetboundaries. A compile-fail example checks that a completed domain cannot outlivemutation of its borrowed graph. The collector covers canonical profiles only;its completion type alone does not certify an original routing master. Cover-relaxation eligibility checks additionally exercise cyclic graphs,fractional cover coefficients, unsupported resource kinds, fixed-route residualmismatches and a shared work/deadline budget. Extra paths excluded by otherconstraints may remain in this relaxation. Cut validity and schedule-dependentrow domination still require separate checks before using a matrix certificate. Cover-row audit tests verify exact partition extrema, rejection of a row thatexcludes a cover, empty versus impossible residual covers, fractional RHScomparisons and state/work/deadline limits. Integer row sums use i128.Failure returns no partial range; a failed relaxed-cover test alone does notprove invalidity under additional fleet or branch restrictions. Resource-boundary regressions cover backward subtraction accepting a path whoseforward additions exceed a window by one ulp. Pricing retries with a freshforward-only engine using the remaining call deadline, recovering valid pathsdisplaced in a bounded candidate pool. Checks cover physical exclusions,topology changes, zero-time stops and an unresolved root without an incumbent.Forward binary64 replay can also reject a path that satisfies exact-real sumsof its input consumptions. These checks establish forward consistency; originalresource-domain certificates need conservative coverage of arithmetic boundaries.The conservative collector has a separate exact-real coverage test, includingan exactly representable sum that nearest/even accumulation rejects. A retainedboundary path also passes the integer row audit and a finite-matrix bound check. Passing these checks establishes the cases exercised by the suite. Benchmarktimings depend on the instance, graph conventions, enabled cuts, backend, andhardware. Preserve that configuration when reporting a performance change.For documentation-only edits, verify local links, API examples, command flags,and option tables without treating a full solver rerun as necessary. Compiled-reference parity tests, binary adapters, fixtures, and tracing tools aremaintained in a separate local workbench outside this Git checkout. They are notrequired by Cargo builds or the regular test suite.

title: Shared master with multiple pricing networks
heading: Shared master with multiple pricing networks
text: Shared master with multiple pricing networks With clp, master::networks::solve solves a fresh root whose pricing graphsshare master rows. Each Network owns a graph, a unique nonnegative ID andfinite nonnegative multiplicity bounds. Local arc IDs may overlap acrossnetworks: route identities include the network ID and resource schedule. Problem.rows defines the shared constraints. Network.arc_entries containsone list of (shared_row, coefficient) pairs per physical arc, in graph order.route_entries adds coefficients charged once per route. The coordinator addsthe network multiplicity rows separately; callers do not include them in theshared-row indices. Arc costs define original route costs. Variable-costmapping used internally by pricing does not modify the supplied graphs.Physical multiplicity rows appear in input-network order: each upper row isfollowed immediately by its lower row when the lower bound is positive. Sharedrows follow these multiplicity rows in their original order. The coordinator maintains independent pricing state, combines columns into onerestricted master and aggregates each network's multiplicity contribution andstabilization subgradient. Output.oracle_calls counts individual oracle calls;Output.master.pricing_calls counts batches. Output.values gives the currentrestricted-master quantity for every route in Output.routes. Phase estimates guide stabilization. Published lower bounds additionally use aresource-free graph-walk relaxation with downward arithmetic. A relevantnegative cycle, arithmetic overflow or unavailable required path leaves thiscertificate unknown. If a complete bound is unavailable, the coordinatorreturns Stalled rather than certifying optimality. Finite artificial penaltiesalso do not certify original-model infeasibility. A stalled restricted LP canstill contain artificial variables; its objective and route quantities arenot then an original feasible solution. The current coordinator accepts fresh roots with an empty initial columnregistry. Cuts, enumeration/MIP transfer, fixed partial solutions and treesnapshots still use the existing single-network workflow and are not yetintegrated here. The scalar resource dimension remains capped at two. Independent checks cover shared covering constraints, fractional and requiredmultiplicities, disabled networks, overlapping local arc IDs, original lowerbounds on generated assignment models and conservative incomplete outcomes: cargo test --features clp --lib master::networks::tests
